diagram_math_checks.objects: Projected coordinate s=omega dot x, time t, extrema a=min supp F and b=max supp F.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local Given supplies a unit omega and nonempty compact supp F. Verification step 3.1 obtains finite attained extrema by F5 and a<b; no new object assumption is required.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The two solid fronts are s=a+ct and s=b+ct, directed toward increasing t and increasing s.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 3.1 proves the translation supp u(t)=supp u(0)+ct omega. Since |omega|=1, projection increases by ct, giving both equations and ds/dt=c>0. A schematic coordinate choice draws both with the same positive slope; numerical plot coordinates do not prescribe a numerical wave speed.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The dashed horizontal slice t=T meets the fronts at a+cT and b+cT.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution into the two equations gives these labels. The literal TikZ intersections are (2.5,1.5) and (4.5,1.5) on the lines from (1,0) and (3,0) with equal displacement (2.8,2.8). Tick marks are centered on those exact intersections.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The intervening region is only the enclosing slab; it is not asserted to equal the support.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Verification 2.1 gives exact support by s-ct in supp F, and 3.1 gives a+ct<=s<=b+ct. Remarks explicitly preserve possible gaps, with no filled region or extra assertion of interval support.

diagram_math_checks.relation: For n>=2 the unpictured transverse hyperplanes remain unbounded.
diagram_math_checks.justification: For fixed allowed s, x=s omega+y with y perpendicular to omega has omega dot x=s. Thus F(s-ct) is independent of all transverse coordinates, exactly as the original Example and Verification state. The diagram projects onto s and claims no compact spatial slab.

diagram_math_checks.relation: No graph-cycle or open/closed ring convention is asserted.
diagram_math_checks.justification: This is a space-time schematic with two axis arrows, two front arrows, one dashed time line and two solid intersection ticks. There are no named-node graph paths or endpoint rings requiring cycle closure; the solid fronts agree with the closed enclosing slab from step 3.1. Arrowheads indicate continuation toward future time, not open endpoints.
